title: Erase Inside: region lock drifts per pointermove (locks to the PREVIOUS cursor sample, not the gesture start) — erases neighboring fills it should never touch
description:
VERIFIED with repro. Flash 8 Erase Inside erases ONLY the fill in which the eraser gesture STARTED, stopping at its boundary for the whole drag; starting on empty erases nothing.

BUG: StageArea.tsx:3230-3233 passes insideAt: sweptStage[0] to planarEraseShape for EVERY move increment — sweptStage[0] is the PREVIOUS pointer sample of that increment, not the pointerdown point. As the drag proceeds the lock point follows the cursor: once the cursor crosses into a different fill, the next increment locks to THAT fill and erases it.

REPRO (confirmed on origin/main b4430b6): red fill 0..100, blue fill 100..200 (adjacent, merged). Simulating the second move increment of a drag that started in red — planarEraseShape(shape, buildEraserStamp([{105,50},{115,50}],8), {mode:'inside', insideAt:{105,50}}) — erases BLUE at (110,50) (fill=null after). Real Flash 8: a gesture started inside red never touches blue.

COMPOUNDING: the lock is re-derived per increment from the CURRENT (already-eroded) shape, whose faces have just been erased/refilled (see task 1425), so the locked component is unstable drag-long. The engine already confines correctly when given the true gesture start (task 1399 connectedFillComponent); only the UI wiring feeds it the wrong point. Shell.tsx:1730 handleEraseOnLayer (agent bridge) uses points[0] of the batch, which is correct for a one-shot batch but the interactive path is per-increment.

SUGGESTED FIX: capture the gesture start point at pointerdown (StageArea.tsx:2206-2228, e.g. eraserGestureStartRef) and pass THAT as insideAt for every increment; better still, resolve the locked connected component ONCE at pointerdown from the pre-gesture shape and pass a face predicate, so mid-drag topology changes cannot re-lock.

ACCEPTANCE: unit/integration test simulating a multi-increment drag (chained planarEraseShape calls exactly like the StageArea loop) that starts in fill A and sweeps into adjacent fill B: A loses only the swept area inside A; B is byte-identical. Also: gesture starting on EMPTY canvas erases nothing in inside mode.

Related: 1399 (engine-side keying, done), 1387 (mode UI wiring), 1425 (hole refill). Found by brush/eraser Flash-8 fidelity audit.
